look_here_first: Find many small YELLOW RADIATE heads crowded in roughly level or rounded terminal clusters. Confirm with pale whitish phyllaries lacking green nerve borders and longer DISC-floret pappus scales; compare Gutierrezia texana and Amphiachyris amoena before naming.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, narrow, linear to oblanceolate, often becoming reduced upward.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Many tiny yellow RADIATE heads with separate ray florets and central disc florets, usually in crowded corymbiform flat-to-rounded arrays on terminal branches. Do not call discoid: Flora of North America and UT Austin describe rays + discs.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: 12–15 involucral phyllaries with pale/whitish resinous faces, 1-veined without a narrow GREEN BORDER along the dorsal nerve (unlike sometimes-green-nerved Gutierrezia texana). Need a true macro to teach this.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypselae with a pappus of scales.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Yellow RAY and DISC florets, not discoid

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Disc pappus has long basally united scales (verify under hand lens)
